scenario: Kate tries to tell one simple story at lunch but keeps digressing — every detail sparks a 'which reminds me...' aside, so the episode is full of non-defining relative clauses, sentential 'which', whose, and reduced (participle) relatives. Kate: 'So yesterday I met David, who runs the New York office — which reminds me, he still owes Pol a yoghurt.' Den, whose desk is nearest the door, keeps trying to steer her back. 'The café we went to, which had just reopened, was packed.' A reduced relative slips in: 'The man sitting by the window turned out to be an old classmate, which was a lovely surprise.' Alex, bored, times how long the story takes. Peter, taking notes, loses track. Warm, funny rambling; the actual point is tiny. Use clearly: non-defining clauses (commas, who/which/whose), sentential 'which' commenting on a whole clause, and a couple of reduced relatives. B2, but keep each sentence readable.
